record.original_question: Let P_n be the path on n vertices, let P_n x P_n be the Cartesian-product grid graph, and for any connected finite graph G define a connected set to be a vertex subset whose induced subgraph is connected. Let N(G) be the number of connected sets, S(G) the sum of their cardinalities, A(G)=S(G)/N(G), and D(G)=A(G)/|V(G)|. What is the limit of D(P_n x P_n) as n tends to infinity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite connected graph $G=(V,E)$, call a subset $S\subseteq V$ a connected set if the subgraph of $G$ induced by $S$ is connected (the empty set is excluded). Let
\[ N(G) = \#\{S\subseteq V : S \text{ is a nonempty connected set of } G\}, \qquad S(G) = \sum_{S} |S|, \]
where the sum is over all nonempty connected sets $S$ of $G$. Define the average connected set size $A(G) = S(G)/N(G)$ and the density $D(G) = A(G)/|V(G)|$.

Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices, and let $P_n \square P_n$ denote the Cartesian product of $P_n$ with itself (the $n\times n$ grid graph, with vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}^2$ and edges between vertices differing by $1$ in exactly one coordinate).

Determine
\[ \lim_{n\to\infty} D(P_n\square P_n). \]
artifact.status_search_result: The asymptotic density of the n×n grid graph for the average connected set size is stated as an open problem. Recent work (2024–2025) gives sharp upper bounds on the number of connected sets in grid graphs and explicit formulas for 3×n and 4×n strips, but does not resolve the limit of D(P_n □ P_n).
